summary: Checks whether a value is convertible to a number.
description: A finite number, or a string that converts to one. `NaN`, the infinities and the empty string are excluded, which is what separates this from a bare `Number(value)`.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is convertible to a number; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
isNumberLike(1); // => true
isNumberLike("1.5"); // => true
isNumberLike(" 42 "); // => true
isNumberLike(NaN); // => false
isNumberLike(Infinity); // => false
isNumberLike(""); // => false
isNumberLike(null); // => false
```
